LESSON: PHONOLOGICAL AWARENESS: PRONUNCIATION

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.1: Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we greet one another?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use appropriate words to introduce self and others

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: PHONOLOGICAL AWARENESS: PRONUNCIATION
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation helps you succeed in ARABIC LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: PHONOLOGICAL AWARENESS: PRONUNCIATION
Study Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Use appropriate words to introduce self and others

What this means
In this part you learn to use appropriate words to introduce self and others. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use appropriate words to introduce self and others.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use appropriate words to introduce self and others. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: use appropriate words to introduce self and others)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: use appropriate words to introduce self and others.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we greet one another?
2. How does pronunciation affect fluency?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: use appropriate words to introduce self and others.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
